messages:
alina: heads up - seeing slow pod start times in us-west2 for GPU jobs. queues piling up, scheduler reports 'binding timeout'. looks like warm slots not coming up evenly across AZs. ~15 pods Pending >10m

sam: on it. any repro or a specific deployment?

alina: all gpu-rt small batch workers. nodeSelector: gpu=true, podAntiAffinity requiredAcrossZones. pasted kubectl describe for one pending pod below:

```
kubectl describe pod gpu-worker-7b9c
Name:         gpu-worker-7b9c
Namespace:    ml-batch
Node:         <none>
Status:       Pending
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age                From               Message
  ----     ------            ----               ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         12m                default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ml-batch/gpu-worker-7b9c to <none>
  Warning  FailedScheduling  11m (x20 over 11m) default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient gpu.com/1, 4 node(s) had taint {no-preempt: true: }, 3 node(s) had affinity that didn't match
```

scheduler-bot: Auto-scale check: warm pool fill rate=0.2 nodes/min in us-west2-a; target=2 nodes/min. Warm pool size=1 (min=1), pending queue=15.

jin: sounds like two things: (1) warm pool not filling fast enough in us-west2-a (maybe spot limits), (2) several nodes in pool have no-preempt taint and our pods require non-tainted nodes. combined = scheduler can't place even though capacity exists in other AZs.

sam: confirming spot capacity window - us-west2-a has constrained spot offers last 30m, us-west2-b/c show spare GPUs. BUT the deployments have strict anti-affinity across AZs which pins scheduling to prefer us-west2-a. that preference is causing retries instead of falling back.

alina: can we do a quick workaround to unblock? relax zone anti-affinity to preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoringDuringExecution?

sam: quick commands:

To patch deployment to preferred affinity (safe canary):
```bash
kubectl patch deploy gpu-workers -n ml-batch --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"affinity":{"podAntiAffinity":null}}}}}'
```
OR better: patch to preferred rule:
```bash
kubectl apply -f - <<YAML
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gpu-workers
  namespace: ml-batch
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 50
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchExpressions:
                    - key: app
                      operator: In
                      values:
                        - gpu-workers
                topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
YAML
```
Also manual scale up warm pool in us-west2-a (infractl):
```
infractl pool scale --region us-west2 --az a --count 4
```

ops-bridge: created INF ticket INF-712 to provision ephemeral capacity in us-west2-a (ephemeral g5 pool). ETA ~45m. https://infra/tickets/INF-712 :construction:

jin: long-term ideas: (a) scheduler plugin to prefer cross-az placement for small gpu jobs, (b) prewarm a lightweight kubelet/daemonset image in each AZ without taints so pods can land quickly, (c) adjust warm-pool allocation policy to spread by predicted zone shortfalls.

alina: i'll run the canary now: patching one deployment to preferred affinity + scale=2 and watch bind times. will report back in ~10m.

sam: thanks. if that doesn't help we can temporarily redirect low-latency traffic to eu-west (not ideal) but prevents user-visible queueing. keep channel posted.

(alina after 14m): alina: update: patch helped. 9/15 Pending -> Running within 3m after warm pool scale. warm pool filling rate improved after infra scale. still seeing a few tainted nodes causing 2 pods to bounce. INF-712 tracks cleanup and a follow-up runbook.

alina: resolving here but follow-up actions: add preferredDuringScheduling for this workload, add warm-pool AZ distribution metric to console, and schedule a deeper postmortem in eng-platform sync. :thumbsup:
